security_audit.summary: The static command-execution alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced curl examples, not executable skill code. The real risk is intentional live email sending through Mailtrap API and SMTP, including bulk paths and token use. No prompt injection or unauthorized exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Live email sending can affect real recipients and sender reputation.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before generating production send commands, and direct non-delivery tests to sandbox workflows.

remediation.issue: Mailtrap API tokens are required for API and SMTP sending.
remediation.suggestion: Store tokens in environment variables, avoid pasting token values into prompts or source files, and rotate exposed tokens immediately.

remediation.issue: Bulk and Campaigns workflows can create compliance risk.
remediation.suggestion: Use verified domains, consented recipients, unsubscribe handling, and Mailtrap suppressions for promotional email.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable guidance when adding live email delivery to an application. This skill explains Mailtrap Email API, SMTP, batch, bulk, and SDK options.
actual_capabilities: Compare Mailtrap Email API, SMTP, batch, bulk, and Campaigns paths.
Identify the correct Mailtrap endpoint for transactional and bulk sending.
Explain SMTP host, port, username, and token settings for live sending.
Guide API token header usage and stream scope considerations.
Point developers to official Mailtrap SDK repositories and documentation.
Highlight common mistakes when choosing Mailtrap sending methods.
limitations: It does not verify sending domains or configure Mailtrap account settings.
It does not replace sandbox testing guidance for non-delivery workflows.
It does not manage Campaigns audiences, scheduling, or reporting in the Mailtrap UI.
SDK method names can change, so users should confirm details in official SDK README files.

use_cases.title: Add transactional email
use_cases.description: Choose the Email API or SDK path for password resets, receipts, alerts, and app notifications.

use_cases.title: Plan promotional sending
use_cases.description: Separate bulk streams, batch requests, and Campaigns so marketing email uses the correct Mailtrap path.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot delivery setup
use_cases.description: Check endpoints, SMTP settings, token use, and common configuration mistakes during integration reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a sending path
prompt_templates.prompt: I am adding Mailtrap to my application. Help me choose between platform integration, SDK, Email API, SMTP, batch, bulk, and Campaigns.

prompt_templates.title: Review transactional setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Mailtrap transactional email setup. Confirm the stream, endpoint, token handling, and testing approach before production use.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose SMTP configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: My Mailtrap SMTP send is failing. Walk through the live host, port, username, token, domain verification, and common mistakes to check.

prompt_templates.title: Design a bulk sending workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Mailtrap bulk sending workflow for promotional messages. Include stream choice, batch considerations, consent, suppressions, and when Campaigns is better.

output_examples.input: I need to send password reset emails from a new web app.
output_examples.output: Use the transactional stream. Prefer an official SDK when available, store the token in an environment variable, and verify the sending domain first.

output_examples.input: I have 300 different notification messages ready at the same time.
output_examples.output: Use the batch endpoint for multiple messages. Keep the stream transactional unless the content is promotional or marketing related.

output_examples.input: Our team wants promotional email with contact lists and reporting.
output_examples.output: Use Mailtrap Campaigns when contacts, scheduling, and reporting belong in the product. Use the bulk stream only for code-managed promotional sends.

best_practices: Prefer official platform integrations or SDKs before direct HTTP or SMTP.
Keep Mailtrap tokens in environment variables and never paste token values into prompts.
Use the sandbox path for tests that should not deliver real email.
anti_patterns: Using the transactional host for promotional or marketing email volume.
Starting with SMTP for a new application when an SDK or API path fits.
Guessing SDK constructors or method names without reading the current README.

faq.question: Does this skill send emails by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides integration guidance and examples. Users still control credentials, code, and execution.

faq.question: Can I use it for sandbox testing?
faq.answer: Use the related sandbox testing skill for capture-only workflows. This skill focuses on live sending.

faq.question: When should I use SMTP?
faq.answer: Use SMTP only when a legacy stack or hosting platform requires it. Prefer integrations, SDKs, or the Email API first.

faq.question: What is the difference between bulk and batch?
faq.answer: Bulk is a promotional sending stream. Batch is a way to submit many messages in one request.

faq.question: Does it cover Mailtrap templates?
faq.answer: It shows where template UUIDs and variables fit. Use the template-specific skill for detailed template workflows.

faq.question: How should I handle API tokens?
faq.answer: Store tokens in environment variables, use the correct stream scope, and rotate any token that may be exposed.
